# Vendored Spec Bundle: `client-js`

> **This file is generated.** Do not edit it or anything under `vendor/spec/`.
> The next spec update overwrites local changes. See [Updating the mirror](#updating-the-mirror).

The `vendor/spec/` directory in this repository is a read-only mirror of the public EzClassify contract. The
source of record is the [ezclassify/contracts](https://github.com/ezclassify/contracts) repository:
the OpenAPI document, the JSON Schemas, and the conformance corpus all live
there. This repository generates no code from the mirror; its tests read it as
the reference contract.

## What this directory contains

- `vendor/spec/openapi.yaml`: REST API contract (OpenAPI 3.x)
- `vendor/spec/json-schemas/`: JSON Schema files for all engine input/output types
- `vendor/spec/plans/v1/`: conformance test plans (engine-slice and server-slice, tagged by `"slice"`)
- `vendor/spec/fixtures/v1/`: scheme fixtures referenced by conformance plans
- `vendor/spec/recordings/v1/`: canonical engine-output recordings, recorded from EzClassify Runtime and published in the [conformance directory of the ezclassify/contracts repository](https://github.com/ezclassify/contracts/tree/main/libs/conformance)
- `vendor/spec/cache/v1/`: the response cache contract every REST client follows, `CACHE-SEMANTICS.md`, and the plans that measure it in wire trips against the wire corpus
- `vendor/spec/replayer-contract/v1/`: HTTP replayer contract corpus; every language replayer must pass these cases before running conformance
- `vendor/spec/semantic/v1/`: the document-assessment semantic contract, its schema, and the fixtures its cases run against
- `vendor/spec/wire/v1/`: the golden wire corpus, canonical request and response pairs for every operation the REST contract serves, with a manifest naming the contract digest they were validated against
- `vendor/spec/MANIFEST.json`: the bundle digest, the source packages, and an empty generator record, because this repository generates no code from the mirror

## Updating the mirror

To change anything in this bundle, change it in the [ezclassify/contracts](https://github.com/ezclassify/contracts) repository. When
the contract changes, the `ezclassify-spec-bot` GitHub App opens a pull request
here with the new bundle and a fresh copy of this file. Its commits are authored
as `ezclassify-spec-bot[bot]` with a `chore(spec):` subject, and the
`vendor-readonly` workflow rejects any other commit that touches
`vendor/spec/` or `vendor/SPEC.md`.

There is no local command that re-vendors the mirror.

Reviewing a spec update means:

1. Reading the provenance table in `vendor/SPEC.md` to confirm the source commit and the package versions it came from.
2. Checking `vendor/spec/MANIFEST.json`: the recorded `openapiSha256` must match
   `vendor/spec/openapi.yaml`, and the `generators` block and `generatedPaths` must stay empty, because this
   repository generates no code from the mirror.
3. Spot-checking the conformance recordings diff for unexpected behavioral changes.

## What if the client warns about a version mismatch against the server?

The client exposes the contract version it was built against through its
language-specific spec-version accessor, documented in the repository README.
The health call reports the deployment's version in its `engineVersion` field,
which every REST client exposes under its language's spelling of that name,
together with the deployment's build identity.

If the deployment's major.minor version differs from the client's contract
version, the client reports a one-time compatibility warning. Mixed minor
versions are unsupported. This mirror is a contract and test input; it contains
no engine implementation.
